thresholdConflicts.resolution: S124/S125 use 85% for 'strong' topic proficiency (advance action, topic_strength observation), while readiness declares a topic 'Ready for focused review' at 80%. These are different gates: S124/S125 gate a coaching-observation claim; readiness gates a band assignment. The 5% gap means a topic at 82% would be 'Ready' but not 'strong' — reasonable but worth documenting. Unify at 80% for 'strong' or keep 85% for the stricter claim.

MAJOR DRIFT. The coaching layer (S124/S125) declares improvement at delta >= 10, but the trend/cluster layer only classifies 'improving' at delta >= 15 (with 5-14 as 'slightly_improving'). Meanwhile S129 outcome classification uses delta >= 5. Three different values for the same concept. Unify: use 15 as the canonical 'improving' threshold across all subsystems; keep 5 as the 'slight' signal; reserve 10 for coaching-layer 'notable improvement' with explicit labeling.
CONSISTENT across S88 and S113. No drift. Both use delta <= -15.

Coaching layer declares 'strong' at 3 attempts; readiness requires 6 for 'Ready' and 4 for 'Approaching'. This is by design — coaching observations are lower-stakes than readiness-band assignments. Document the tiered approach: 3 = 'can observe', 4 = 'approaching reliable', 6 = 'ready-reliable'.

S124/S125 use recentPct >= 75 as part of the 'improving' coaching claim. Readiness uses >= 80 as 'high' and >= 70 as 'good'. The 75 sits between readiness tiers. Consider aligning S124/S125 to use 70 (matching the 'good' tier) or document that 75 is intentionally between the two readiness bands for coaching.

Three distinct stability tiers exist for different purposes: 60 = 'steady/good enough for approaching', 75 = 'high for ready', 80 = 'well-established for progress insight'. These represent genuine granularity tiers, not drift. The 60/75/80 cascade is intentional. Document as three-tier stability framework.

60% is the canonical 'weak' threshold across all subsystems. 50% is used only for the more severe labels: '(needs work)' in lowest-accuracy fallback and 'contradictory' outcome classification. These are sub-threshold tiers within the overall 'weak' band — not conflicts. Document as 'weak' (60) and 'severe' (50).

Multiple session-count gates exist for different purposes: 1 = can build strategy (minimal), 2 = can compare sessions / show digest, 3 = sufficient for readiness assessment. This is a tiered approach, not drift, but it should be documented as a single progression scale: 1 → basic insights, 2 → cross-session comparison, 3 → readiness assessment.

S127/S128 define 'weekly' as 'last 7 sessions' (session-count-based), while S129 defines '1week' as 7 calendar days. These are different concepts: session-based (activity-triggered) vs. calendar-based (time-triggered). For a learner doing 3 sessions/day, 7 sessions ≈ 2.3 days; for one doing 1 session/week, 7 sessions ≈ 7 weeks. Document both definitions explicitly and consider adding a calendar-based digest alongside the session-based one.

thresholdConflicts.concept: Misconception pattern minimum count for visibility
thresholdConflicts.resolution: Coaching shows misconception patterns at count >= 2; weekly digest and study strategy only recommend focus at count >= 3. This is reasonable tiering: 2 repetitions = 'noticeable', 3 repetitions = 'actionable'. Document as intentional.

thresholdConflicts.concept: Confidence calibration minimum entries (overconfident vs underconfident)
thresholdConflicts.resolution: Overconfident claims require 4 entries; underconfident claims require only 3. Asymmetric threshold — underconfident claims are made with less evidence. Consider unifying at 4 for both, since both are calibration claims that affect learner self-perception.

thresholdDriftInstances.note: Coaching declares 'strong' at 85%; readiness declares 'Ready' at 80%. A topic at 82% is Ready but not Strong — the more conservative coaching layer creates a 5% gap.
CRITICAL DRIFT. Coaching says improving at +10; cluster engine says improving at +15; outcomes say positive at +5. Three different thresholds for the same concept across three layers.
Coaching needs only 3 attempts to call a topic 'strong'; readiness needs 6 for 'Ready'. Intentionally different (lower bar for coaching), but should be explicitly a tiered framework.
Coaching-layer 75 sits between readiness tiers of 70 and 80 — intentionally between the bands but undocumented as such.
Three tiers of stability: 60 (steady), 75 (ready-level), 80 (well-established). Gap of 20 points from lowest to highest — should be documented as a tiered stability model.
One subsystem defines 'weekly' by session count (7 sessions), another by calendar time (7 days). These produce entirely different windows depending on study cadence.
Asymmetric evidence requirements: overconfident needs 4 entries, underconfident needs 3. The more impactful claim (overconfident) has the higher bar — defensible but asymmetric.

missingThresholds: accuracy_medium_range: No threshold defines the 60-70% range — topics in this band are neither 'weak' nor 'strong' and have no dedicated coaching language
stability_medium_range: No threshold for the 50-60% stability band — between 'unstable' (50) and 'good' (60)
recentPct_declining: No explicit threshold for 'recent accuracy is concerning' independent of delta — only delta-based classification exists
hint_rate_threshold: No numeric threshold for 'excessive hint usage' — only trend direction ('increasing') is checked, not absolute rate
time_since_last_session: No threshold for detecting dormant/returning learners based on calendar gap between sessions
topic_coverage_pct: No threshold for 'topic coverage breadth' — e.g., % of CMA blueprint sections with at least N attempts
fatigue_detection: No threshold for detecting accuracy degradation within a single session (e.g., last 5 vs first 5 accuracy)
mastery_plateau: No threshold for detecting when a topic has stopped improving despite continued practice
overstudy_warning: No threshold for detecting when a strong topic is being over-practiced at the expense of weak areas
readiness_confidence_level: No threshold distinguishing 'high confidence' vs 'low confidence' readiness assessments — only a vague 'moderate'/'low' string exists
recommendation: Adopt a single-source-of-truth (SSOT) threshold registry in may-learner-state.js. All coaching functions in may-core.js should read from this registry rather than hardcoding literals. The registry should define: (1) canonical value, (2) tier label, (3) which subsystems use which tier, (4) rationale for any intentional divergence. The getThresholdSnapshot() function (may-learner-state.js:1111) already provides the readiness thresholds — extend it to cover ALL thresholds. Create a THRESHOLD_REGISTRY object at the top of may-learner-state.js that all getter functions and may-core.js coaching functions reference. This eliminates the 11 identified conflicts and 7 drift instances, and gives tests (test_calibration.js) a single point of truth for validation.
